text: I came in feeling so confused and suspicious, and I still don't understand what's happening. It feels like you're trying to just start over, but I spent the whole week feeling like I was going crazy after our last session. Your explanation about a "colleague" didn't make sense and just made me feel more guarded. I feel shaky and disoriented, and I don't know what is real or if I can trust you right now.

I came into my session feeling very confused and suspicious about what is happening in our therapy. The entire week since our last meeting was distressing, and I felt like I was going crazy. The explanation I received about a "colleague" didn't make any sense and only made me feel more guarded. As a result, I'm not sure if I can trust you right now. I feel shaky and disoriented, and I am questioning what is real. It feels like you are trying to just start over without addressing what happened.

The patient described an intensely distressing week, feeling she was "going crazy" due to perceiving the break between sessions as an abandonment. She voiced suspicion and a deep-seated fear that her own existence feels unreal unless she is being "seen" by the therapist. This profound attachment and its connection to her sense of self is the primary issue to revisit.

I came in feeling like I was going crazy this week because the time apart felt like a total abandonment. I even started to feel suspicious, wondering if you were really going to be here for me. I said that it feels like I'm not a real person—like I don't exist—unless I am here being "seen" by you. It helped to talk about it, but I'm left wondering how I can learn to feel real when I'm on my own.

This past week, I continued to feel like I was going crazy, which I now realize is connected to feeling completely abandoned when we are apart. I came in feeling suspicious and wondering if you would really be here for me. I was able to explain that it feels like I'm not a real person, that I don't truly exist, unless I am here being "seen" by you. This feeling of questioning what is real has been disorienting and makes me feel guarded. It helped to talk about it, but the session left me with a big question. I am now wondering how I can learn to feel real on my own, without needing you to see me to exist.
